rendered: Among the aluminium-based entries in Table 5[1], the highest Li-ion diffusivity belongs to amorphous Li3.5Al2O3, at 7.1 ×10^− 10[2] cm^2/s. Amorphous Al2O3 is far lower, at 5.94 ×10^− 17[3] cm^2/s, so the lithiated amorphous phase is several orders of magnitude more diffusive. The other aluminium-based entries sit lower: LiAlO2 at 1 ×10^− 11[4] cm^2/s, Li0.2Al2O3 at 1.1 ×10^− 14[5] cm^2/s, AlF3 (am) at 9.26 ×10^− 16[6] cm^2/s and AlF3 (cry) at 6.2 ×10^− 18[7] cm^2/s. The lithium-rich aluminium oxides diffuse faster than the amorphous Al2O3 parent, in line with the prose's statement that coating oxides with different lithium stoichiometry show higher lithium-ion diffusivity than parent oxides.
